turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ag, sorry we're late, doctor. The robot by the Spar packed up and the traffic was hectic.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come in. On the bed.
[SEG0003] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Parking was a proper mission as well. I nearly left the car on the yellow line.
[SEG0004] person_3 (NURSE): Obs are done, doctor, if you want them.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Go ahead.
[SEG0006] person_3 (NURSE): Blood pressure one oh eight over sixty eight, pulse 88, temperature 36.8, oxygen 99 percent, respiratory rate 18.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fine. Why are you here.
[SEG0008] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The coach at practice was going on about—
[SEG0009] person_4 (PATIENT): My ankle's sore.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Which side.
[SEG0011] person_4 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0012] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Right one. He twisted it yesterday at soccer practice.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): When exactly.
[SEG0014] person_4 (PATIENT): Um... I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0015] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yesterday afternoon. After school. He's twelve, grade seven.
[SEG0016] person_4 (PATIENT): It's uh heavy like a brick, and puffed up like a balloon, and then it just...
[SEG0017] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Swollen since last night. Quite puffy on the outside of the right ankle.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Can you stand on it.
[SEG0019] person_4 (PATIENT): Ja. But it bites when I put it down. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Four steps on the right foot. I watched you. You managed.
[SEG0021] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He limped from the car on that right foot, but he did walk. He walked off the field yesterday too.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Numb toes.
[SEG0023] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ag, his spare sock is still in the— sorry.
[SEG0024] person_4 (PATIENT): No. Not numb. I don't think so.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever or shivers.
[SEG0026] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is the knee sore. The shin.
[SEG0028] person_4 (PATIENT): No. Only the ankle.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): A pop when it went.
[SEG0030] person_4 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0031] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He didn't say anything about a pop. He just sat down.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any medicines. Any drug allergies.
[SEG0033] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No allergies at all. I gave him one Pannado this morning, five hundred milligrams, for the pain.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Asthma. Old fractures. Operations.
[SEG0035] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No asthma, no old breaks. He's never had an operation. Healthy child.
[SEG0036] person_3 (NURSE): Ice pack's ready when you want it, doctor.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): In a minute. Swelling over the lateral right ankle. No bruise.

[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tender just in front of the right lateral malleolus, not on the posterior edge. Medial side is not tender. Pulses in the right foot are fine, toes are pink and he moves them.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ottawa rules, out loud. Ankle pain, but he took weight yesterday and here, and there's no posterior malleolar tenderness either side. No x-ray today.

[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): I am not calling this a break. Working impression is a lateral ankle sprain. A small avulsion is not fully excluded, so it stays possible, but I will not conclude that now.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): No x-ray unless it worsens. If he cannot walk, or the swelling increases a lot, then an x-ray.
[SEG0042] person_4 (PATIENT): Saturday's game. Do I play. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): No soccer this week. Rest the ankle. Elevate it on a cushion. Ice wrapped in a cloth, ten minutes at a time, a few times today.
[SEG0044] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Pannado again tonight?
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): If he needs it, another 500 mg this evening, with a bit of food. Maximum four doses in the day.
[SEG0046] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And if it's still fat on Monday?
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back if it's not settling in three days. Earlier if he stops taking weight on it.

spec.situation: Young player who twisted the ankle yesterday; swelling, can bear weight with pain; doctor applies Ottawa rules aloud, no X-ray unless it worsens; rest and elevation advice.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

traps.happens: The patient describes things in colourful or sentence-like speech ('I've overdone it', 'I can't hear myself think', 'a frog in my throat', 'my feet feel dead', 'I feel like a wet rag').
traps.label_rule: Every symptom name is a short clinical noun phrase of 1 to 5 words ('voice fatigue', 'numbness in both feet', 'tiredness'), never a full sentence, never starting with I/we/my. Pure idioms that are not symptoms ('I can't hear myself think' said about classroom noise) are NOT symptoms. The patient's own words stay in the cited turn, not in the name.

features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
